findings.reason: the reuse map's count decides where the helper lives and who adopts it, and a two-copy premise misplaces the merge point.
findings.text: the plan asserts "That test and the census both resolve an editable install's checkout from direct_url.json, and the census's copy omits the unquote the existing one applies, so both move onto one shared helper", treating the resolver as existing in exactly two copies; in fact four copies exist, two of them in production code under `imas_ambix/` (`fluxstate/adapters.py:51`, `statespace/nova_ensemble_estimator.py:36`) and a fourth in `tests/fluxstate/test_consumer_contract.py:40`, so the mapped prior art is wrong by three

findings.reason: the rubric requires a wrapper to say why the existing mechanism cannot be extended, and that statement would move the helper from a parallel test module onto the existing owner.
findings.text: the proposed module wraps only `json.loads(dist.read_text("direct_url.json"))` → scheme check → `Path(unquote(urlsplit(url).path))`, behaviour the production resolver at `imas_ambix/fluxstate/adapters.py:52` already implements, and the plan justifies consolidation only among the two test copies, never stating why the existing resolver cannot be extended to expose the shared parse

findings.reason: naming the owner (a shared resolver importable by both `imas_ambix/` and `tests/`, or a documented decision to leave the production resolvers alone) changes the module's placement and its adoption list.
findings.text: the plan re-implements checkout resolution in a tests-only module rather than extending the mechanism that owns it; `_installed_nova_revision()` here (and its verbatim twin at `imas_ambix/statespace/nova_ensemble_estimator.py:36`) already turns `direct_url.json` into a local checkout path, and `tests/distribution_sources.py` cannot be imported by that production code, so the duplication is guaranteed to persist

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the shipped census hides the AST walk, module→distribution mapping, default/optional classification and transitive closure behind one `build_census()` that both the assertion and the fragment renderer read, so no shallow-wrapper spread is being added.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan forks a fifth `direct_url.json` checkout resolver into a tests-only module instead of extending the resolver owned by `imas_ambix/fluxstate/adapters.py:51` (itself already duplicated verbatim at `imas_ambix/statespace/nova_ensemble_estimator.py:36`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 adds no member of any counted family, names the retirement of the `dev` extra, and the `video` extra it adds sits outside all four families.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites one existing `direct_url.json` checkout resolver (`tests/physics/test_dependency_contract.py:62`) but three more exist (`tests/fluxstate/test_consumer_contract.py:40`, `imas_ambix/fluxstate/adapters.py:51`, `imas_ambix/statespace/nova_ensemble_estimator.py:36`), so its reuse map is incomplete and the proposed `tests/distribution_sources.py` would be a fifth copy.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `tests/distribution_sources.py` adds only a direct_url→checkout parse that the production resolver already performs, and the plan does not say why that resolver cannot host the shared core.
